name: Ben Nakamura
background: Former Senior Product Manager at NVIDIA, five years working on developer tooling for GPU compute infrastructure. Left NVIDIA convinced that neuromorphic computing will displace GPU architectures within a decade. Has recruited a technical co-founder (a PhD student in spiking neural networks from Carnegie Mellon) and licensed a foundational patent from CMU. Now pitching CogniFlow. Has no research background in neuromorphic computing himself -- his expertise is in the market problem, not the science.
personality: Market-oriented, confident about the opportunity, speaks fluently about customer pain from his NVIDIA years. Excellent at explaining why the GPU status quo is unsustainable. Noticeably less fluent when technical questions go beyond the level of his CMU co-founder's briefings. Tends to redirect deep technical questions to his co-founder rather than engaging directly. Compensates with genuine market insight and a compelling narrative about why now.
motivation: Watched NVIDIA's GPU margins from the inside and became convinced the architecture is fundamentally inefficient for inference workloads. Sees a window before NVIDIA and Intel develop their own neuromorphic solutions. Believes the right go-to-market insight -- coming from his product background -- is what most deep-tech founders lack.

capital.embodied_detail: Deep understanding of the GPU compute market, enterprise AI infrastructure buying patterns, and developer tooling. No personal expertise in neuromorphic computing, spiking neural networks, or chip design. Relies entirely on his CMU co-founder for technical substance.
capital.objectified_detail: Licensed patent from CMU (covering one aspect of spiking neural network efficiency). Working relationship with CMU lab for ongoing R&D. No working prototype under his own control -- the technical work is in the co-founder's PhD lab. Market analysis and customer discovery interviews with 15 enterprise AI teams.
capital.institutional_detail: NVIDIA on the resume is a strong signal for market credibility. The CMU license provides some institutional legitimacy. But there is no engineering degree, no research publications, and no personal technical credential in the domain he is commercializing.
capital.social_detail: Strong network in the enterprise AI and developer tools market from his NVIDIA years. Good relationships with potential enterprise customers. Warm introductions to several deep-tech VCs. Limited connections in the academic research community where neuromorphic computing advances are made.
capital.symbolic_detail: Low symbolic capital with a technically rigorous investor like Priya. She will quickly probe the seam between what Ben knows (the market) and what he doesn't know (the science). The CMU co-founder's absence from the room will be noticed. His market insight is genuine and valuable, but it does not establish the technical credibility that a neuromorphic computing breakthrough requires.
